label: Code interpreter / calculator tool
newbieExplainer: Instead of the model doing arithmetic 'in its head', it writes a small program that a sandboxed Python actually runs, then reads the result. The model only needs to plan the calculation — the computer does the computing.
caveat: Requires the model to be decent at tool calling — check that dimension first.

label: MCP / external tools
newbieExplainer: MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets the model call outside services — web search, file access, calculators — so it doesn't have to rely on what it memorized.
caveat: Also depends on the model's tool-calling ability.

label: RAG (retrieval)
newbieExplainer: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: your documents are searched first, and the relevant passages are pasted into the prompt, so the model answers from your data instead of guessing.
caveat: Quality depends heavily on how the documents are chunked and searched.

label: Move up a quant band
newbieExplainer: Quantization compresses the model to fit in less memory, but the smallest versions lose real ability. If your machine has headroom, a 4–5 bit file often recovers most of what a 3-bit file lost.

label: Prompt technique
newbieExplainer: Some weaknesses shrink if you ask differently — e.g. 'think step by step', giving an example of the output format you want, or splitting a big request into smaller ones.

label: Update your runtime
newbieExplainer: Brand-new model architectures often need brand-new runner code. If a fresh model produces garbage or won't load, the fix is frequently just updating llama.cpp / LM Studio / Ollama to a build that supports it — not a different quant.

label: No known fix — choose a different model
newbieExplainer: Some weaknesses are baked into the model itself. No tool or trick meaningfully changes them, so we say so instead of pretending a workaround exists.
